Fiona — the famed Nile hippopotamus at the Cincinnati Zoo — will be honored at Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade on Thursday, one week after her death.

Volunteers handling the Macy’s blue hippopotamus balloon — which last appeared at the parade in 1931 — will be wearing purple patches in a small tribute to Fiona, the department store chain said in a statement.

“Fiona brought joy to millions, including so many in the Macy’s community in Cincinnati,” the statement read.

“This year, as Macy’s welcomes our own beloved Blue Hippo back to the Parade, we wanted to mark Fiona’s memory.”

The beloved 9-year-old hippo — whose premature birth and early fight for survival captured hearts around the world in 2017 — died from complications after she ingested a hat that mistakenly fell into her habitat.

The hat was deep in her small intestine and no supportive care could have prevented her death, the zoo said in a statement.

In the days since her death, tributes have poured in at the zoo, elsewhere in Cincinnati and beyond.

On the same day of Fiona’s death, Macy’s unveiled a blue hippo-themed holiday window at its New York City store in a nod to the 1931 balloon which — like others at the time — was cut loose following the parade.

Despite a public effort to find it, it was the only balloon from that parade that the store never recovered.

The department store chain said it got the Cincinnati Zoo’s blessing for volunteers to wear the Fiona patches and made a donation to the zoo in her memory.
